newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS-US Robotics busy as stock falls.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS-US Robotics busy as stock falls.

text.p: U.S. Robotics Corp put options were active in morning trading on Thursday as the stock fell sharply.
Options traders could not pinpoint a reason for the stock drop, but they said possible explanations making the rounds included a decline in the modem business and stiffer competition.
"There are lots of rumors but no one really knows," one trader on the floor of the Chicago Board Options Exchange said. "There are a lot of put buyers."
U.S. Robotics officials were not available for comment.
One analyst said he thought momentum investors were exiting the stock.
By 1100 CDT (1600 GMT), U.S. Robotics shares were down 2-15/16 at 46-3/4 on volume of more than four million shares.
The stock fell as low as 46-1/2 in choppy early trading.
The U.S. Robotics puts were the fourth most active on the American Stock Exchange, led by the September 50s, which traded nearly 1,200 contracts.
The September 50 put, which had open interest of 4,844 through Wednesday, was ahead 1-1/4 at four.
On the CBOE, the September 50 put was most active, with about 650 contracts changing hands.
"There's good volume for out-of-the-money puts," one trader said of the September 45 puts. He added that October volume was relatively thin.
Marty Kearney at PTI Securities noted that volatility on the U.S. Robotics put options picked up on the stock selloff.
He explained that, for instance, volatility on the September 45 puts was up to around 68 from a historical 63.
"We've just been selling," one options trader said, adding that his firm had been selling small blocks in both the puts and the calls.
In consolidated trading, U.S. Robotics September 45, 50 and 55 calls were relatively active, with the 45 trading about 500 contracts, the 50 about 800 and the 55 roughly 550.

Among the calls, the November series saw some action, from the 45 strike through to the 65. Also, some trading was seen in the November 70 calls, the 75 calls, 77-1/2 calls and the 82-1/2 calls. --G. Crawford, (312) 408-8750/E-mail: derivatives@reuters.com
